title: A Witness for the Letter
premise: When twin letters arrive at the cathedral archives—one a murder confession, the other a taunting promise of more—Marguerite Lockridge realizes the crimes mirror a fifteen-year-old cold case she herself filed away, and that the writer knows her filing system intimately. Partnering with Detective Ines Okonkwo, who carries her own guilt over the original case, Marguerite must reconstruct the crypt's sealed history while dodging a killer who anticipates every archival move. The trail leads to a beloved found family of cathedral volunteers whose loyalty was forged around a shared sin, and Marguerite must choose between exposing them and protecting the only home she's ever had. In the end, she uses the killer's obsession with the file against him—planting a false record that lures him into the locked crypt, where memory, love, and duty finally collide.
about_author: Coral Quintana is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing diocesan archives in coastal New England before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries obsessed with the quiet violence of paperwork and the families we build in old buildings.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Establishes her meticulous life among the cathedral archives and her ritual of alphabetizing the town's dead. A quiet, melancholy opening that shows her found family of volunteers and ends with the arrival of two envelopes postmarked the day of a murder.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Marguerite reads the confession letter and its sinister twin promising 'more, in order.' Her hands shake as she recognizes the handwriting style from an old case file. Fear and a strange thrill of being seen. Ends with her calling the police.

chapters.title: Detective Okonkwo, Fifteen Years Late
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She arrives at the cathedral carrying guilt over the unsolved 2009 killing her father investigated. She and Marguerite clash over protocol versus archival instinct. The beat: two women with different kinds of guilt circling the same wound.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She reveals the crypt beneath the cathedral has been sealed since 2009 by order of the diocese. The letters reference something only visible inside. Ines obtains a warrant. Dread builds as the seal is broken.

chapters.title: What the Cold Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Inside the crypt they find the original victim's effects arranged in alphabetical order—someone has been tending the scene for fifteen years. Horror and awe. Marguerite realizes the killer is one of her own volunteers.

chapters.title: The Tuesday Circle
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Introduces the volunteer family: organist Theo, sexton Bram, widow Cressa, and teenager Junie who files with her on Tuesdays. Marguerite studies each face, wondering which one is lying. Warmth laced with paranoia.

chapters.title: A Second Letter, A Second Body
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A second murder, staged exactly as the letter promised. The victim is a former cathedral accountant who audited the crypt fund in 2009. The killer is working through a list Marguerite unknowingly created.

chapters.title: File 14-C
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She pulls the original cold case file and discovers pages missing—pages she filed herself. Memory of the night she catalogued them is foggy. Guilt and self-doubt: did she lose them, or did someone take them through her?

chapters.title: Junie's Alphabet
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The teenager adores Marguerite and notices a stranger asking about the archives last month. She keeps a secret notebook. The beat: found family from the youngest angle, and the first hint the killer studied Marguerite's routines.

chapters.title: The Confession That Doesn't Fit
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Forensics show the confession letter's handwriting matches the dead accountant—not the killer. The letters are forged from a template. The killer is quoting documents, not writing them. Rising dread: the file itself is the weapon.

chapters.title: Cressa's Candles
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She visits widow Cressa, who lights candles for a name no one else remembers. Cressa almost speaks, then retreats. Marguerite leaves with the sense that the volunteers share a covenant older than her fifteen years.

chapters.title: The Bishop's Quiet Order
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The diocese pressures the department to close the crypt and the case. Ines suspects institutional cover-up. Duty versus truth theme crystallizes. She chooses to keep working off the books, with Marguerite.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Missing Year
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A fragment returns: the night in 2009 when she catalogued the file, someone stood in the archive doorway. She'd assumed it was Bram. Memory as unreliable ally. Emotional beat: the horror of not trusting your own past.

chapters.title: Theo's Fugue
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The organist plays the requiem from the 2009 funeral and realizes he can't remember the week of the murder—dissociated trauma. He suspects himself. Sympathy deepens even as suspicion spreads through the circle.

chapters.title: Letter Three
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A third letter arrives, addressed not to the police but to 'The Archivist, who keeps us in order.' The killer flatters her system and names the next victim by their file number. Marguerite feels horrifyingly complicit.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Behind a crypt niche, Ines finds a ledger of payments into the cathedral's restoration fund—donations that don't match any bank record. Someone laundered money through the church, and the 2009 victim found it.

chapters.title: What Bram Carries
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The old sexton confesses privately to Marguerite that he sealed the crypt—not on the bishop's orders, but to protect 'the children of this house.' He won't say more. Loyalty versus truth; Marguerite's found family fractures.

chapters.title: The Trap That Was Set for Her
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She realizes the killer's letters have been steering her to specific files—the case is a guided tour only she can read. She's not a witness; she's an instrument. Fear turns to fury, and fury into resolve.

chapters.title: Ines's Father's Notes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. She finally reads her late father's notebooks on the 2009 case and finds he suspected the restoration fund too—and died before he could prove it. Grief and inheritance of duty. She and Marguerite formally ally.

chapters.title: The Volunteer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Records reveal a former volunteer, 'Elias Vane,' who left in 2009—whose identity traces to a dead child. The killer has been wearing a fictional life for fifteen years. The investigation narrows to who he truly was.

chapters.title: Junie Follows the Stranger
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Junie spots the stranger from her notebook near the crypt entrance and follows, nearly becoming a victim. She escapes but loses her notebook in the chase. Guilt and terror; the killer now knows the circle's youngest member.

chapters.title: The Ransom of the Notebook
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A letter offers to return Junie's notebook 'when the file is complete.' The killer is holding the girl's trust hostage. Marguerite must decide whether to keep Junie away or use her as bait—love against duty in miniature.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Suspects
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Ines together. They map every volunteer against the ledger, the letters, and the 2009 timeline on the archive floor. The system that once comforted Marguerite now indicts everyone she loves. The beat: the file is a mirror.

chapters.title: Cressa Breaks the Covenant
chapters.summary: Cressa's POV. The widow finally confesses: in 2009 the circle covered up an accidental death in the crypt—a boy fell during a secret restoration job—and the fund paid for silence. The 'murder' was staged to hide the accident. The truth inverts.

chapters.title: The Boy in File 14-C
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The missing pages named the dead boy—and his guardian, who was never told how he died. The killer is the guardian, avenging a cover-up by executing the alphabet of everyone who filed it away. Marguerite understands him; that's the horror.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Duty
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The DA wants to charge the volunteers for the cover-up, which would give the killer exactly the confession he wants, in public. Ines must choose legal duty or the trap. She chooses the trap—and risks her badge.

chapters.title: The False Record
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She and Ines plant a forged file: 'the complete ledger, held in the crypt, to be read aloud Sunday.' The killer's obsession with order will force him to come for it. Marguerite grieves corrupting her own archive. Sacrifice beat.

chapters.title: Junie's Notebook, Returned
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The notebook reappears on her desk, pages annotated in the killer's hand—praising her filing. He's telling them the trap worked and that he's watching the child. Maternal panic ripples through the whole circle.

chapters.title: Vigil
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, braided. Saturday night: Ines and officers hidden in the crypt, Marguerite in the archive as bait, the volunteers keeping an unwitting vigil upstairs. Stillness before the storm; each character makes a private vow.

chapters.title: The Man Who Filed Himself
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The killer comes for the false record—and Marguerite recognizes him at last: the quiet man who repaired the archive's binding machines, the one person she never filed because he was always simply there. Betrayal of the most domestic kind.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The killer seals the crypt with Ines inside, mirroring the boy's death—he wants an investigator to die the same way, filed and forgotten. Cat-and-mouse in the dark among the niches. Claustrophobic midpoint climax.

chapters.title: Marguerite Opens the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She breaks her own rule—she has the only other crypt key, kept 'off the record'—and opens the seal. Duty to the archive yields to love for Ines. The killer escapes into the cathedral above; Ines is saved but the hunt is live.

chapters.title: Requiem, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. During Sunday service the killer takes the organ loft, forcing the congregation to hear the boy's name read into the record. Theo plays against him—a battle of music and memory. The town finally learns what it buried.

chapters.title: The Confession He Wanted
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The killer corners Bram in the bell tower, demanding a public confession. Bram begins to give it—truth as surrender. Ines negotiates, offering the real ledger and prosecution instead of execution. The tower standoff tightens.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She reveals her final card: the original missing pages were never lost—she hid them in 2009 because they implicated the boy's guardian in the cover-up's payoff. Her fifteen years of secrecy made her the killer's perfect instrument. Devastating self-reckoning.

chapters.title: The Reading of the File
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the crypt, before the killer, Marguerite reads the true record aloud—every name, including his and the boy's—giving the dead their order at last. He lowers the weapon not because he's defeated, but because he's finally been filed. Grief and catharsis.

chapters.title: Arrest in the Archive
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The arrest is quiet, almost liturgical. The killer asks only that his letters be kept in order. Ines chooses to charge the volunteers too—duty honored—but advocates for mercy given the cover-up's origins. Justice with a human face.

chapters.title: Re-Cataloguing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later, she rebuilds the archive, creating a new file: 'The Vane Case, complete.' Junie returns on Tuesdays. Bram and Cressa await trial; Theo plays again. The beat: a found family broken but not disbanded, learning to be honest.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Crypt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The diocese, under new leadership, unseals the crypt permanently and dedicates a memorial to the boy. Marguerite leaves flowers in alphabetical order, then—deliberately—out of it. Memory honored, order released.

chapters.title: A Letter for the Archivist
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing. One last letter arrives: from the killer, from prison, a single line—'Thank you for keeping us.' Marguerite files it, then writes back, the first letter she's ever sent. Love, duty, and memory reconciled; the door of the archive stands open.
